setup: Hinge down and pick up the weight on one side
Stand tall with your shoulders level
Arm long, weight just clear of your leg
execution: Brace and walk with short, steady steps
Stay tall; don't lean either way
faults: Don't lean away from or into the weight
Don't rest the weight against your leg

notes: Pick the weight up and put it down with a hinge: flat back, weight close to your body.
Clear the walkway first, and set the weight down rather than drop it.
Grip usually gives out first. Put the weight down before it slips.
The logged load is the one dumbbell or kettlebell. Carry the same distance with each hand.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Lighter weight, shorter distance
regressions.reason: Learn to walk tall without leaning before adding load.

progressions.name: Heavier weight or longer distance
progressions.reason: Add one at a time while the posture stays level.

substitutions.name: Farmer's carry
substitutions.reason: A weight in each hand; more total load, less sideways challenge.

substitutions.name: Kettlebell front-rack carry
substitutions.reason: Loaded walk with the bells held at the chest.

substitutions.name: Side plank
substitutions.reason: Same side-of-waist work as a static hold.

substitutions.name: Pallof press
substitutions.reason: Trunk work that resists twisting, when there's no room to walk.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Front view at waist height so any sideways lean shows. The figure walks in place toward the camera (no floor scroll); one dumbbell in the right hand, left arm relaxed.

keyPositions.label: Right step
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall, shoulders level, right arm long with the dumbbell just clear of the thigh. Right foot stepping forward a short step. Torso vertical; no lean toward or away from the weight.

keyPositions.label: Left step
keyPositions.describe: Same tall, level posture with the left foot stepping forward. Dumbbell and right arm unchanged.

ikHints: Shoulders and hips stay level in every frame
Dumbbell hangs straight down from the shoulder, clear of the leg
emphasise: Weight held just clear of the leg
